pr_title: reimplement ansible-galaxy login with OAuth Device Flow
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
The GitHub username/password auth API that `ansible-galaxy login` currently uses is deprecated and will be removed in November (https://developer.github.com/changes/2020-02-14-deprecating-oauth-auth-endpoint/). Once the current GitHub UI is removed, `ansible-galaxy login` will no longer function to manage an ambient user credential in `~/.ansible/galaxy_token`.

There are two short-term options:
* Remove support for interactive token generation from the `ansible-galaxy` CLI
    * This requires users to always pass `--token` (or set the `ANSIBLE_GALAXY_TOKEN` envvar) for all `publish` operations (and any future functionality that requires being auth'd to a Galaxy/AH server). The token to pass must be retrieved from the Galaxy profile UI in the browser.
* Reimplement `ansible-galaxy login` on a supported GitHub API
    * This allows users to continue to have an "ambient" Galaxy credential instead of explicitly passing a token on all operations requiring auth

The [GitHub OAuth Device Flow beta](https://docs.github.com/en/developers/apps/authorizing-oauth-apps#device-flow) provides a reasonable replacement for the old API (and also works with 2FA and other browser-compatible auth methods). 

This PR implements an OAuth Device Flow client:
* User runs `ansible-galaxy login` (against a configured server or default `galaxy.ansible.com`)
* CLI prompts user to visit https://github.com/login/device/code in a browser and enter an 8 character code. If not already logged into GitHub in the browser, they'll first be prompted to auth to GitHub using whatever mechanisms are available on their account (including 2FA/OTP, which didn't work with the old CLI auth)
* CLI polls device code for user completion, then retrieves the ephemeral user token and send it to the Galaxy server, creating and storing a Galaxy token under `~/.ansible/galaxy_token` (as it did before)
* Further calls to `ansible-galaxy role|collection publish` use the stored auth token

Known issues:
* We don't have a good way to get the Galaxy server's OAuth `client_id` to pass to GitHub - this is a blocking problem that needs to be solved (though we could just hardcode them for well-known Galaxy servers to make it work for now). It's "sort of" available if we scraped the Galaxy Login UI (as Galaxy eventually creates a redirect to the GitHub login UI that includes it on the query string), but would be very brittle to changes in redirect behavior.
* There's no great way to do automated testing of this behavior in our current CI system, since it requires live GitHub credentials and browser automation to close the device auth loop.

fixes #71560

- Feature Pull Request

ansible-galaxy login

I'm not sure where the `ansible-galaxy cli command documentation comes from (https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/cli/ansible-galaxy.html#role-login) but can you make any necessary changes there as well?

The only comment I have is that we should be pushing people towards putting the token into a config file, not passing it on the command line via --token.  Anything passed via command line args is insecure so --token should really only be used for testing purposes.  For production work, reading it from a config file or out of the environment are the secure options.

Fully agree with @abadger

For my automated test&publish workflows I need some way of non-interactive login which doesn't require me to store the secret in the (public) git repo.

And if possible _not_ device bound, as these workflows run in ephemeral docker containers

> For production work, reading it from a config file or out of the environment are the secure options

reading from a config is already supported.

* https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/reference_appendices/config.html#galaxy-token
* https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/reference_appendices/config.html#galaxy-token-path
* https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/galaxy/user_guide.html#configuring-the-ansible-galaxy-client

@sivel just an FYI the first 2 config options are actually your GitHub token which is used for the login command and not your Galaxy token. The 3rd one is the correct way of setting the token in the config though.

We've not gotten any user feedback advocating for the preservation of this feature from many different channels polled, so for now we're just going to kill the feature. We'll add a descriptive error message to `ansible-galaxy login` that enumerates the remaining options for token auth (CLI, envvar, `~/.ansible/galaxy_token`). If there's major user blowback after it's released, we can always resurrect this PR, and hopefully a future version of Galaxy can support OAuth Device Flow natively, at which point we could bring this back as an authority-agnostic option.

My point is, please *do not* enumerate cli as a way to work around this
feature going away.  It's insecure and should only be used when testing
that a workflow works.  Not when trying to use authenticated Ansible-Galaxy
commands for production usage

##### SUMMARY
`ansible-galaxy login` uses the OAuth Authorizations API which is going to be deprecated on November 13, 2020. Any applications authenticating for users need to switch to their newer methods: https://docs.github.com/en/developers/apps/authorizing-oauth-apps#device-flow

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
<!--- Write the short name of the module, plugin, task or feature below, use your best guess if unsure -->
ansible-galaxy login

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
This affects all versions.

##### CONFIGURATION
<!--- Paste verbatim output from "ansible-config dump --only-changed" between quotes -->
```paste below

```

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
<!--- Provide all relevant information below, e.g. target OS versions, network device firmware, etc. -->
This affects all environments.


##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
Everything still works today, but will fail in about 10 weeks.

There are brownout times when we should see failures to login via the CLI.

The brownouts are scheduled for:

    September 30, 2020
        From 07:00 UTC to 10:00 UTC
        From 16:00 UTC to 19:00 UTC

    October 28, 2020
        From 07:00 UTC to 10:00 UTC
        From 16:00 UTC to 19:00 UTC

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
<!--- Describe what you expected to happen when running the steps above -->
Today login works with a user's Github username and password, as long as that user has not enabled 2FA.

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
On November 13 this method will no longer work and no user will be able to authenticate via Github, which is the only authentication mechanism we have for the current version of Ansible Galaxy.

This is *not* an issue we can resolve on the Galaxy side, it has to be resolved in the client.

review_comments: Is a class really needed if the initialized is not parametrized?
If this needs to be done in two months we may want to keep this emitting a warnings until then, so that the bugfix versions of Ansible would warn users at least for some time...
I think we are actually leaning toward not "fixing" this, and just having `ansible-galaxy login` error, and give instructions for manually getting the token from the galaxy UI.
This should probably make use of `self._code_resp['expires_in']` to save an API call that is guaranteed to fail.

`machine-man` is not related to the device auth flow (it used to be necessary for GitHub Apps).

Besides, they've made those APIs stable already: https://developer.github.com/changes/2020-08-20-graduate-machine-man-and-sailor-v-previews/.
